newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian shares outperform in Q4, year - ANZ.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian shares outperform in Q4, year - ANZ.

text.p: Australian shares outperformed other major asset classes during the December quarter and the past calendar year, Australia and New Zealand Banking Group (ANZ) said in its latest ANZ Investment Monitor publication released on Sunday.
Australian shares rose 7.2 percent in the three months to end-December and 14.6 percent during 1996, the bank said.

Solid returns were also achieved in the other major asset classes during the quarter with international shares returning 4.3 percent (in Australian dollar terms), fixed interest 3.4 percent and Australian property 3.2 percent.
Cash returned 1.5 percent, while gold was the worst performing asset, falling 2.8 percent.
In calendar 1996, fixed interest yielded a return of 11.8 percent, Australian property 10.7 percent, cash seven percent and international shaers 6.7 percent.
Gold fell 11 percent over the year.
ANZ Fund Management's chief investment officer, Glenn Woolley, said in a statement that over the past 10 years, residential property outperformed all the major asset classes.
Fixed interest and cash also outperformed Australian and international shares during the decade.

"Progressively lower inflation during the past 10 years has allowed interest rates to fall, which has resulted in significant capital gains in the bond market, contributing to the fixed interest market's total return (income plus capital gains)," Woolley said in a statement.

"This phenomenon is not expected to repeat itself for a long time. However, if inflation is kept under control, the fixed interest market should provide sound real rates of return in the long term," he said.
Woolley said international and Australian shares should regain top position in the performance stakes in the long-term.
